caption: LUM-1267 interaction assertions (120x34), revised by LUM-1271 for the post-LUM-1261 wrapping layout. Run against a binary built from feature/pi.rs; every panel asserts the interaction a codex/pi-class TUI owes the user.
notes: Assertion kinds: expect/reject gate the run; probe records A/B evidence (XFAIL when a binary does not have a behaviour yet); xfail/xfail_reject are markers for known defects and fail the run when they unexpectedly pass.

Panels 3-4 document the completion filter's over-broad candidate set (LUM-1260 §2): `mo` matches substring in the description too, upstream matches the name only, so those needles are xfail_reject — they must move to `reject` when LUM-1263 lands.

LUM-1271 revision (why panels 15-18 differ from LUM-1267's original 15-17): LUM-1261's wrap fix (c8bc6785a) made the /help and /hotkeys bodies wrap per source line instead of being hard-clipped at the right margin, so each block is now taller than the ~11 transcript rows a 34-row frame leaves after the expanded startup header. A bottom-anchored log therefore shows the block's TAIL, and the old head needles ('slash commands:', 'Ctrl+L open the model selector', ...) can only pass on the pre-fix renderer that silently truncated every row (e.g. '... /exit quit the interactive session keys: Enter submit promp'). The head needles are not dropped: they move to the two <Home> panels (16 / 18), which assert the same content is REACHABLE by scrolling. Panels 15/17 additionally `reject` the pre-fix clipping artifacts, so this gate fails on the b5769b585 baseline and passes on the merged tip - measured both ways in LUM-1271's docs/TUI_*.md.
Panel 8 is legitimately byte-identical to panel 6 (closing the model-selector overlay returns to the same placeholder frame); the harness prints that as a WARN, not a failure.

Column padding is part of the wrapped layout: the aligned rows are '·   <key><pad><text>', so the needles here deliberately start after the padding ('open the model selector', not the pre-fix 'Ctrl+L open the model selector' which was the unaligned clipped form). Rows are newline-joined and right-stripped, so a needle must fit inside one row; the wrapper breaks on whitespace, so single tokens such as '/thinking' survive any break.

panels.label: 1. idle: product line, hint table, onboarding line, composer placeholder, status line
expect: Pi can explain its own features

panels.label: 2. type / -> the command completion opens with a live counter and the first candidate selected
3. type mo -> /model stays selected and the over-broad candidate set is visible (see the xfail_reject markers)

xfail_reject.text: Copy last agent message to clipboard
xfail_reject.why: LUM-1263: upstream filters candidates by command name only; matching the description too is a deviation and must go

xfail_reject.text: Create a new fork from a previous user message

panels.label: 4. Down -> the selection marker moves to the next candidate and the counter agrees
5. Tab -> the selected candidate is applied to the composer and the list closes

reject.why: the completion list must be gone once a candidate is accepted

panels.label: 6. Enter -> the slash command runs and reports its result in the transcript
7. /model + Enter -> the model selector overlay lists real models with their providers
8. Esc -> the overlay closes and the composer is back to its placeholder
9. @ -> file-path completion over the fixture tree, with paths resolved relative to the cwd
10. src -> candidates narrow to that subtree; the unfiltered fixtures are gone
11. Tab -> the path token is composed into the composer and the list closes
12. a real turn through the provider: the prompt and the reply both land in the transcript
13. !bash -> the command, its output and its duration are reported as one tool block
14. Ctrl+O -> the status line reports the tool-output expansion state
15. /help -> the wrapped reference renders; the bottom-anchored log shows its tail and no row is hard-clipped at the right margin

reject.why: pre-fix the 32 source lines were clipped into 11 hard-cut rows and a cut landed inside a word ('promp'); this needle only exists in that truncated rendering

panels.label: 16. Home -> window 1 of the reference: the command table's head is reachable (needles are kept off the window edges: the window shifts by a row when the bash block renders one line more)
17. PgDn -> window 2 of the reference: the middle of the command table is reachable
18. /hotkeys -> the chord table renders bottom-anchored; the tail is on screen and not hard-clipped

reject.why: the pre-fix clip landed exactly there ('... / accept autocomplete commands: / slash'); the needle spans the cut, so it can only match the truncated rendering

panels.label: 19. PgUp -> one page back and the chord table's app + selector sections are there
20. End then PgUp -> the log follows the bottom again and scrolling back brings up the jump-to-latest pill
